## Install[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

This page covers every install route. Next: [Quick start](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

Run Booster from inside the app you want to upgrade: `--path` defaults to `.`, so `booster plan` needs no flags. Booster needs PHP 8.3 or newer on the machine; the app it upgrades does not, because Rector runs from Booster's own `vendor/`.

### Single file (PHAR)[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#single-file-phar)

```
mkdir -p ~/bin
curl -L -o ~/bin/booster.phar https://github.com/waynestate/booster/releases/latest/download/booster.phar
alias booster='php ~/bin/booster.phar'    # put this line in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to keep it
cd /path/to/your-app
booster detect
booster plan
booster run --dry-run
booster run
```

`detect` reads the app and prints its type and versions. `plan` lists the steps. `run --dry-run` previews the edits and changes nothing. `run` edits files and makes no commit. A real `run` also needs git, a clean git folder (commit or stash first) and a Docker daemon for its test gate.

### Linux, macOS and WSL (Ubuntu): clone it[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#linux-macos-and-wsl-ubuntu-clone-it)

```
sudo apt install php-cli php-xml php-mbstring php-zip php-curl unzip git composer
```

Ubuntu splits the XML extension out of `php-cli`, and Composer's dev dependencies need it: when Composer says "ext-dom is missing", run the line above. On macOS: `brew install php composer git`. Ubuntu 22.04 ships PHP 8.1, too old for Booster: add the [ondrej/php PPA](https://launchpad.net/+ppas?field.name=php&field.status=active) or use the Docker route below. Then:

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster && composer install
bin/booster --version
```

Run Booster from its own folder with `--path` pointing at the app; never clone Booster inside an app:

```
bin/booster plan --path=/path/to/your-app
```

`--path` takes a path, and a leading `~` means your home folder (from `HOME`, or `USERPROFILE` on Windows). In WSL, keep Booster and the app in your Linux home folder, not under `/mnt/c` (a Windows drive is slow from Linux); a Windows folder is `/mnt/c/Users/<you>/...`, and `run` needs Docker Desktop's WSL integration switched on.

### Windows PowerShell, with PHP and Composer installed[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#windows-powershell-with-php-and-composer-installed)

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster; composer install
php bin\booster --version
php bin\booster plan --path=..\my-app
```

### Docker only, no PHP (Windows or any OS)[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#docker-only-no-php-windows-or-any-os)

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -w /booster composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -v "/path/to/app:/app" -w /booster php:8.4-cli php bin/booster plan --path=/app
```

Run these from inside the booster folder.

This route can run `detect`, `plan`, `scan` and `run --dry-run`. A real `run` starts Docker and uses git from inside Booster, which the `php:8.4-cli` image lacks, so for a real run use the single-file or clone route (in WSL on Windows). When Booster itself runs in a container, pass `--skip-gate` to `run` and run the tests yourself. Node hops run `npm` in a `node:26` container, so they need the same daemon but no Node installed on the machine.

Booster prints its progress lines on standard error. In Windows PowerShell they print in red, as if they were errors. They are not errors; the exit code tells you whether the run worked.

Booster is also on Packagist as `waynestate/booster`: give it its own folder, not your app's `vendor/`, because it needs PHP 8.3 even when your app doesn't. Clone it as above, or run `composer create-project waynestate/booster booster ^1.0`.

### Single-file download[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#single-file-download)

Booster ships as a single-file PHAR, so Preflight and apps without Composer access can run it as one file. The first route above downloads it; every version tag publishes the same `booster.phar`: the GitLab release carries it as an asset, and the GitHub release at github.com/waynestate/booster carries it as an attachment. Run it with `php booster.phar`.

You can also build it from any commit, with the script for your OS (both need Docker, and no PHP or Composer on the host):

Windows (PowerShell):

```
.\scripts\build-phar.ps1
```

Linux / macOS:

```
scripts/build-phar.sh
```

Each script writes `build/booster.phar` and verifies it by printing Booster's version.

Every command works from the phar. `detect`, `plan`, `hops` and `init` read only what is bundled inside it. `run` copies Rector, its `config/rector.php` and `docker/` out of the phar into a temp directory first, because Rector and `docker build` are child processes that cannot be pointed at a `phar://` path; the temp directory is removed when the command exits.

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/next.html

## Next[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/next.html#next)

This page lists what Booster does not do yet, and what it decided not to build. It is the only place future work lives; the other pages describe what ships today.

### Open[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/next.html#open)

- **The gate needs a real app.** The contract tests cover the bundled example apps. A full `run` against a real Wayne State application with the gate on has not been proven in CI yet; the proof site carries those runs.

### Decided not to build[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/next.html#decided-not-to-build)

- **An MCP server for Booster.** App owners drive upgrades from their own machines and CI; an MCP endpoint would add a surface to secure without a caller that needs it.
- **Automatic merge requests.** Booster edits a working copy and stops. Opening MRs on app repositories would make a tool that fixes code into one that ships it, and the person reading the diff is the point of the review threshold.

### Not built yet[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/next.html#not-built-yet)

- **Custom rules.** Apps sometimes need a rewrite Rector does not ship. Booster has no way to register one yet; until it does, such rewrites stay manual.
- **Pilot numbers.** No pilot cohort has run yet, so there are no counts of apps upgraded or hops applied to publish.
- **A `cas-to-sesame` run against a real app.** The hop exists (opt in with `--sesame`) and renames the classes, swaps the Composer requirement, writes `config/sesame.php` from the old config and rewrites the model trait. Duo two-factor stays manual work, and the hop has not been run against a real app yet.

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html

## How do I...[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#how-do-i)

This page answers "how do I use Booster for X?" one situation at a time. Each recipe has the command, what Booster will do, and when to reach for something else. For the default behavior (no flags at all), read [What a run does by default](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-a-run-does-by-default) first. For every option, see [Commands](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html). Replace `../my-app` with your app's path.

Two things hold for every recipe:

- `plan` and `run` take the same options, so you can try any flag on `plan` first. `plan` changes nothing.
- A real `run` needs the app under git with a clean working copy, plus Docker for the test gate. A dry run needs neither.

### 1. Just look first[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#1-just-look-first)

You want to know what the app is on and what moving it would take, before anything changes.

```
booster detect --path=../my-app
booster plan   --path=../my-app
booster plan   --path=../my-app --format=json
```

`detect` reads `composer.json`, `composer.lock` and `package.json` and prints the app type, PHP, Laravel, PHPUnit, Vue, Node and Boost. `plan` prints the numbered hops, the warnings and the advisory scans. `--format=json` gives the same plan as JSON for scripts. None of the three changes a file.

Not for: finding what will break on a given PHP. That is `booster scan --php=<target>`, also advisory.

### 2. Go all the way to current[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#2-go-all-the-way-to-current)

You want the newest PHP and Laravel CREED's policy supports, and you are happy to take it a hop at a time.

```
booster run --path=../my-app
```

With no flags Booster plans one hop per PHP minor, Laravel major and PHPUnit major up to the policy's newest, plus the front-end Node hops. It runs them in order, tests the app after each one, and stops at the first red gate. It never commits. A Laravel 10 app on PHP 8.1 plans 11 hops; a PHP 5.5 app with no framework plans 12 hops to PHP 8.5. The long version is in [What a run does by default](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-a-run-does-by-default).

Not for: an app with no tests and no one to click through it afterward. The gate then only proves every file still parses, which is a start and not a finish (see recipe 10).

### 3. Only get off an old PHP, or reach a specific PHP[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#3-only-get-off-an-old-php-or-reach-a-specific-php)

You want PHP 8.4, say, and you would rather not change anything else.

```
booster run --path=../my-app --to-php=8.4
booster run --path=../my-app --goal=php-74-to-84
```

`--goal=php-74-to-84` is shorthand for `--from-php=7.4 --to-php=8.4`; use it (or `--from-php`) when `composer.json` has no usable `php` constraint.

What happens depends on the app:

- **No framework:** you get the PHP hops from the current minor to the target, plus a PHPUnit step wherever PHP allows one. Nothing else moves.
- **Laravel app:** passing only `--to-php` does not freeze Laravel. The Laravel target still defaults to the newest the policy supports, so Booster plans the Laravel hops too, or stops with an error such as "Laravel 13 does not run on PHP 8.2" when that newest Laravel cannot run on the PHP you asked for. To move PHP and leave Laravel alone, name the Laravel you are on:

```
booster run --path=../my-app --to-php=8.3 --to-laravel=10
```

Booster checks the pair against what Laravel supports and refuses one it does not (for example, a PHP the Laravel you are on cannot run on). Passing any target also leaves the Node front-end hops out, with a warning (recipe 7).

Not for: getting a Laravel app current. Laravel and PHP limit each other, so the interleaved default plan is the safe path.

### 4. Reach a specific Laravel major[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#4-reach-a-specific-laravel-major)

```
booster plan --path=../my-app --to-laravel=12
booster run  --path=../my-app --to-laravel=12
```

Booster plans the Laravel hops up to that major and adds the PHP hops that Laravel needs along the way; the PHP target is still the policy's newest unless you also pass `--to-php`, and a pair Laravel does not support is an error. PHPUnit follows the newest major that runs on the target PHP, raised to at least the floor your target Laravel ships with. A target older than the app is an error.

Not for: stopping at a Laravel major that is past security support as a destination. Booster warns and treats it as a stop on the way up.

### 5. One hop at a time, for small reviewable merge requests[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#5-one-hop-at-a-time-for-small-reviewable-merge-requests)

You want each hop as its own commit, so a reviewer reads one diff at a time.

```
booster plan --path=../my-app                  # note the id of hop 1
booster run  --path=../my-app --only=<hop id>  # run that one hop
git -C ../my-app diff                          # review it
git -C ../my-app add -A && git -C ../my-app commit -m "<hop id>"   # commit; the tree is clean again
```

Then go round again: `plan` now starts from the new versions, so its first hop is the next one. `--only` must name the first hop of the current plan, because the app has to sit on that hop's starting versions; Booster says so plainly otherwise. `--until=<hop id>` is the coarser tool: it keeps that hop and every hop before it, which suits "do the PHP part today, Laravel next sprint". `--only` and `--until` cannot be combined.

Not for: hops that depend on each other more than you expect. Hops are ordered for a reason; a bigger batch with `--until` is fine when the hops in it are boring.

### 6. Preview without changing anything[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#6-preview-without-changing-anything)

```
booster run --path=../my-app --dry-run
```

Rector shows the diffs it would make, hop by hop, and nothing is written. No git or Docker is needed, and the baseline and gate are skipped. The limit: a Laravel hop needs the app's own `vendor/` to see Laravel's classes. With no `vendor/`, that hop's preview is marked incomplete (run `composer install` first). With a `vendor/` from an older Laravel, a later Laravel hop reports "Can't preview" because it needs the earlier hops applied. Preview one hop at a time with `--only`, or apply the earlier hops for real and dry-run again.

Not for: proving the app still works. A preview never runs your tests.

### 7. Backend only, or front end too[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#7-backend-only-or-front-end-too)

Node front-end hops (the Node pin, Mix to Vite, Vite major, Tailwind, TypeScript, the Vue steps and Inertia 3) are in the plan only when you pass no target at all. Two ways to leave them out:

```
booster run --path=../my-app --to-php=8.5          # any target drops them, with a warning
booster run --path=../my-app --skip=mix-to-vite    # or drop them by id
```

`plan` lists the left-out ids in its warning. To keep them while passing a target, add `--with-node`:

```
booster run --path=../my-app --to-php=8.5 --with-node
```

The ids are `node-pin-24`, `mix-to-vite`, `vite-major`, `tailwind-3-to-4`, `typescript-major`, the Vue steps and `inertia-2-to-3`; `booster hops` lists every id. Skipping `vue-2-to-3` skips all the Vue steps.

Not for: skipping the Node hops and then keeping a Mix build around forever. That is a choice, not a plan.

### 8. Skip a hop you will do by hand[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#8-skip-a-hop-you-will-do-by-hand)

```
booster run --path=../my-app --skip=<hop id>
```

`--skip` can be repeated. The hop leaves the plan and Booster plans the rest around it; an unknown id is an error that tells you so. Some hops are marked `[manual: you do this one by hand]`: those are playbooks, and Booster does not do them for you. Do any hop you skip before the hops that depend on it, or the later gates will tell you.

Not for: skipping to dodge a red gate. Fix the cause, or use recipe 14.

### 9. A big app[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#9-a-big-app)

A hop that would change more than 200 files stops to ask you first. In a terminal you see the per-rule summary and a prompt; with `--no-interaction`, in CI, or with `--format=json`, the run stops at that hop instead of asking nobody.

```
booster run --path=../my-app --max-changes=500   # apply a hop up to 500 files, no prompt
booster run --path=../my-app --max-changes=0     # no limit
booster run --path=../my-app --memory-limit=4G   # more memory for Rector (default 2G, -1 for none)
```

`--max-changes` is a hard limit per hop: a hop over it changes nothing and says so. Read the summary before you raise it.

Not for: lifting the limit everywhere to make the prompt go away. The prompt is the review.

### 10. Tests and the gate[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#10-tests-and-the-gate)

The gate is your app's tests, run in the target PHP's Docker image after every hop. Options for every kind of app:

```
booster run --path=../my-app --allow-failing-baseline
booster run --path=../my-app --test-command="vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Unit"
booster run --path=../my-app --test-env=DB_CONNECTION=sqlite --test-env=APP_ENV=testing
booster run --path=../my-app --image=my-registry/php-apache:{php}
booster run --path=../my-app --skip-gate
```

- **No tests:** the gate runs a built-in `php -l` check on every PHP file outside `vendor/` and `node_modules/`. It proves the code parses, not that it works. [A smoke test for WSU apps](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/smoke-test.html) gets you a real gate.
- **Tests already red:** the baseline (your tests on the current PHP) stops the run before hop 1. `--allow-failing-baseline` goes on anyway and labels later failures as pre-existing. See [The baseline](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baseline.html).
- **Custom test command:** `--test-command` replaces the default (`composer test`, else `vendor/bin/phpunit`, else the syntax check).
- **Environment for the tests:** `--test-env KEY=VALUE`, repeatable. The report names the keys only, never the values.
- **Your own image:** `--image` takes one image name, a `{php}` template, or a map such as `8.1=foo:1,8.2=bar:2`; the image needs `php` and `composer` on `PATH`, and must cover every PHP in the plan.
- **Few tests, but pages that must not change:** `--replay` records how the app answers a list of requests before the first hop and fails any hop that changes an answer. `booster replay init --path=../my-app` drafts the request file. See [The replay gate](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/replay-gate.html).
- **Skip the gate:** `--skip-gate` skips the baseline, the per-hop tests and the PROCTOR check.

Not for: `--skip-gate` on a real upgrade. The gate is how you learn which hop broke the app. Use it only when Docker truly cannot run, and then run the tests yourself after each hop.

### 11. Offline, or a dirty working copy[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#11-offline-or-a-dirty-working-copy)

```
booster plan --path=../my-app --no-package-check
booster run  --path=../my-app --allow-dirty
```

`--no-package-check` skips the Packagist dependency check, so `plan` works with no network (you lose the report of which direct dependencies block which hops). `--allow-dirty` lets a real run start with uncommitted changes. The default refuses so that the upgrade diff stands alone and `git checkout .` can undo it; with `--allow-dirty` that undo would also throw away your own edits, so commit or stash if you can.

Not for: running on an app that is not in git at all. Booster wants the change to be reversible; put the app under git first.

### 12. Move off wayne-cas to SESAME, or WayneUI 1 to 2[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#12-move-off-wayne-cas-to-sesame-or-wayneui-1-to-2)

Both moves are opt-in:

```
booster plan --path=../my-app --sesame
booster plan --path=../my-app --wayneui
booster run  --path=../my-app --sesame --wayneui
```

Without the flag, `plan` only warns that your app uses `wayne-cas` or WayneUI 1.x and tells you the flag to add. `--sesame` needs the app to require `cit-web-infra/wayne-cas` and a plan that reaches PHP 8.3; it lands just before the Laravel 10 to 11 hop. `--wayneui` needs the app to require `cit-web-infra/wayne-ui` and a plan that reaches Laravel 11. If the plan ends below those, the move is left out with a warning, and Booster says why.

### 13. Plan for a future date, or a different policy[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#13-plan-for-a-future-date-or-a-different-policy)

```
booster plan --path=../my-app --today=2027-06-01
booster plan --path=../my-app --policy=/path/to/policy.json
```

The default target is "the newest the policy supports on the plan's date". `--today` pins the date (format `YYYY-MM-DD`), so a plan is repeatable and you can see what a later date would ask of you. `--policy`, or the `BOOSTER_POLICY` environment variable, points at a different CREED `policy.json`; the default is the copy in the `waynestate/creed` package.

Not for: a real run on a faked date. Dates are for planning; run on the real one.

### 14. After a stop[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/recipes.html#14-after-a-stop)

A run stops at the first hop that fails (a red gate, a hop over the file cap, a Composer error) and reports the rest as "not run". The report names the hop, the phase (Composer or tests), and the last lines of output. The failed hop's changes stay in place so you can read them; `git checkout .` undoes them.

The usual loop:

1. Read the report for the failing hop.
2. Fix the cause: the code Rector could not fix, a package that blocks the hop, a test that depends on old behavior. `plan` shows which direct dependencies block which hops.
3. Commit the fix on its own, so it is reviewable.
4. Run again. Booster reads `composer.json` fresh each time, so it plans from the versions the app is on now and the finished hops are not repeated.

If you would rather throw the failed hop away, `git checkout .`, fix the cause, and run again. To get the hop's edits and keep working in the same tree, pass `--allow-dirty`.

Not for: re-running again and again hoping for a different answer. Booster is deterministic; the gate will be just as red.

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

This page lists every command and option Booster takes; the table is generated from the tool by the docs build. With no flags, `detect`, `plan` and `run` start from what Booster finds in the app and climb to the newest PHP and Laravel the policy supports; see [What a run does by default](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-a-run-does-by-default).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `booster detect` | Say which of the five stack permutations an app is, and its PHP, Laravel and Vue versions. |
| `booster hops` | List every hop BOOSTER knows. |
| `booster init` | Write the coding-tab playbooks (.agents/skills). With --check, fail when they are stale. |
| `booster plan` | Show the ordered hops from the app to a supported version. Changes nothing. |
| `booster replay` | The replay gate on its own: init drafts booster-replay.json, record saves how the app answers now, check fails when an answer changed. |
| `booster run` | Run the plan: Rector, composer.json edits and a test gate per hop. Edits the working copy only. |
| `booster scan` | Advisory scans: show what will break on a PHP version, and what PHPStan says there. Changes nothing. |

#### `booster detect` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-detect)

Say which of the five stack permutations an app is, and its PHP, Laravel and Vue versions.

Usage: `booster detect [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster hops` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-hops)

List every hop BOOSTER knows.

Usage: `booster hops [--format FORMAT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster init` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-init)

Write the coding-tab playbooks (.agents/skills). With --check, fail when they are stale.

Usage: `booster init [--path PATH] [--dir DIR] [--check]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--dir=VALUE` | Skills directory (default: /.agents/skills). |  |
| `--check` | Change nothing; exit 1 when a playbook is missing or out of date. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster plan` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-plan)

Show the ordered hops from the app to a supported version. Changes nothing.

Usage: `booster plan [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--policy POLICY] [--today TODAY] [--goal GOAL] [--from-php FROM-PHP] [--to-php TO-PHP] [--from-laravel FROM-LARAVEL] [--to-laravel TO-LARAVEL] [--to-phpunit TO-PHPUNIT] [--with-node] [--sesame] [--wayneui] [--skip SKIP] [--no-package-check] [--until UNTIL] [--only ONLY] [--no-scan]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--policy=VALUE` | Path to CREED's policy.json (default: BOOSTER_POLICY, then the waynestate/creed package). |  |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--goal=VALUE` | Shorthand such as php-74-to-84: sets --from-php and --to-php. |  |
| `--from-php=VALUE` | The PHP version the app runs on (major.minor). |  |
| `--to-php=VALUE` | Target PHP version (default: the newest the policy supports). |  |
| `--from-laravel=VALUE` | The Laravel major the app runs on. |  |
| `--to-laravel=VALUE` | Target Laravel major (default: the newest the policy supports). |  |
| `--to-phpunit=VALUE` | Target PHPUnit major (default: the newest that runs on the target PHP). |  |
| `--with-node` | Include the Node front-end hops (Node pin, Mix to Vite, Vite major, Tailwind, TypeScript, Vue) even when you passed a target version |  |
| `--sesame` | Include the wayne-cas to SESAME swap. |  |
| `--wayneui` | Include the WayneUI 1.x to 2.x move. |  |
| `--skip=VALUE` | Hop id to leave out (repeatable). |  |
| `--no-package-check` | Skip the Packagist dependency check (for offline use). |  |
| `--until=VALUE` | Cut the plan after this hop id: that step and everything before it stay. |  |
| `--only=VALUE` | Plan and run just this one hop id; the app must sit on the hop's starting versions. |  |
| `--no-scan` | Skip the advisory scans (PHPCompatibility and PHPStan). |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster replay` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-replay)

The replay gate on its own: init drafts booster-replay.json, record saves how the app answers now, check fails when an answer changed.

Usage: `booster replay [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--file FILE] [--recording RECORDING] [--php PHP] [--image IMAGE] [--out OUT] [--no-install] [--force] [--] <action>`

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | yes | init, record or check. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--file=VALUE` | The request file, relative to the app or absolute. | `booster-replay.json` |
| `--recording=VALUE` | Where record saves the answers and check reads them, relative to the app or absolute. | `booster-replay.recording.json` |
| `--php=VALUE` | The PHP version to serve the app on (default: the version the app declares). |  |
| `--image=VALUE` | Serve the app in this Docker image instead of booster-target, in the same three forms as run --image. |  |
| `--out=VALUE` | Folder for the transcripts (default: a new booster-replay-- folder in the system temp folder). |  |
| `--no-install` | Do not run composer install first; use the vendor/ the app already has. |  |
| `--force` | init only: overwrite an existing request file. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster run` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-run)

Run the plan: Rector, composer.json edits and a test gate per hop. Edits the working copy only.

Usage: `booster run [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--policy POLICY] [--today TODAY] [--goal GOAL] [--from-php FROM-PHP] [--to-php TO-PHP] [--from-laravel FROM-LARAVEL] [--to-laravel TO-LARAVEL] [--to-phpunit TO-PHPUNIT] [--with-node] [--sesame] [--wayneui] [--skip SKIP] [--no-package-check] [--until UNTIL] [--only ONLY] [--dry-run] [--max-changes MAX-CHANGES] [--test-env TEST-ENV] [--memory-limit MEMORY-LIMIT] [--skip-gate] [--image IMAGE] [--allow-failing-baseline] [--allow-dirty] [--test-command TEST-COMMAND] [--proctor-command PROCTOR-COMMAND] [--proctor-advisory] [--replay [REPLAY]] [--replay-out REPLAY-OUT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--policy=VALUE` | Path to CREED's policy.json (default: BOOSTER_POLICY, then the waynestate/creed package). |  |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--goal=VALUE` | Shorthand such as php-74-to-84: sets --from-php and --to-php. |  |
| `--from-php=VALUE` | The PHP version the app runs on (major.minor). |  |
| `--to-php=VALUE` | Target PHP version (default: the newest the policy supports). |  |
| `--from-laravel=VALUE` | The Laravel major the app runs on. |  |
| `--to-laravel=VALUE` | Target Laravel major (default: the newest the policy supports). |  |
| `--to-phpunit=VALUE` | Target PHPUnit major (default: the newest that runs on the target PHP). |  |
| `--with-node` | Include the Node front-end hops (Node pin, Mix to Vite, Vite major, Tailwind, TypeScript, Vue) even when you passed a target version |  |
| `--sesame` | Include the wayne-cas to SESAME swap. |  |
| `--wayneui` | Include the WayneUI 1.x to 2.x move. |  |
| `--skip=VALUE` | Hop id to leave out (repeatable). |  |
| `--no-package-check` | Skip the Packagist dependency check (for offline use). |  |
| `--until=VALUE` | Cut the plan after this hop id: that step and everything before it stay. |  |
| `--only=VALUE` | Plan and run just this one hop id; the app must sit on the hop's starting versions. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Show the diffs Rector would make and change nothing. |  |
| `--max-changes=VALUE` | Hard limit on files changed per hop, with no prompt (0 = no limit). Without it, a hop over 200 files asks first, or stops when not interactive. |  |
| `--test-env=VALUE` | Environment variable (KEY=VALUE) passed to the baseline and every gate container with -e; repeat it. Values never appear in the report. |  |
| `--memory-limit=VALUE` | Memory limit for the Rector process (for example 2G), or -1 for no limit. | `2G` |
| `--skip-gate` | Do not run the tests in the target image after each hop, or the PROCTOR check at the end. |  |
| `--image=VALUE` | Run the gate in this Docker image instead of building booster-target (it needs php and composer on PATH): one name for every PHP version, a {php} template such as registry/php-apache:{php}, or a map such as 8.0=foo:1,8.1=bar:2. |  |
| `--allow-failing-baseline` | Continue even when the baseline (the app's tests on its current PHP) fails; later gate failures are labeled as pre-existing. |  |
| `--allow-dirty` | Run even when the working copy has uncommitted changes. |  |
| `--test-command=VALUE` | Command that runs the app tests inside the image (default: composer test, else vendor/bin/phpunit). |  |
| `--proctor-command=VALUE` | Extra command run in the image after the tests, for example a PROCTOR check. |  |
| `--proctor-advisory` | Report the PROCTOR result but do not fail the run on it. |  |
| `--replay=VALUE` | Also gate on request replay: record how the app answers before the first hop, replay after each hop, fail on a changed answer. Takes the request file (default: booster-replay.json). |  |
| `--replay-out=VALUE` | Folder for the replay transcripts (default: a new booster-replay-- folder in the system temp folder). |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `booster scan` [#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#booster-scan)

Advisory scans: show what will break on a PHP version, and what PHPStan says there. Changes nothing.

Usage: `booster scan [--path PATH] [--php PHP] [--removals] [--format FORMAT] [--phpstan]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--php=VALUE` | The PHP version to ask about (major.minor). |  |
| `--removals` | List uses of functions and constructs removed in PHP up to --php, instead of the PHPCompatibility scan. |  |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format (text, json). | `text` |
| `--phpstan` | Also run the PHPStan scan (Pinstripe preset) at the same PHP version. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

Example: an app moving from Laravel 8 to 13 takes the climb in parts. `booster plan --path=../my-app --until=laravel-8-to-9` keeps every hop up to and including the move to Laravel 9, and `booster run` with the same flag applies exactly those hops.

### Exit codes[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` the baseline failed, a hop was capped, errored or failed its gate, or the PROCTOR check found new findings, `2` bad usage (bad option, unreadable policy, broken `composer.json`, a target the policy does not know).

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html

## Configuration[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

This page lists the environment variables Booster reads; the table is generated by the docs build.

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BOOSTER_BOT_TOKEN | Push token for the hop data robot (bin/hop-data-bot.php). Never in git, never logged, never printed | none | src/Refresh/HopDataBot.php |
| BOOSTER_POLICY | Path to CREED's policy.json | none (uses the snapshot bundled with BOOSTER) | bin/refresh-hop-data.php |

Booster reads the policy straight from the `waynestate/creed` package in its own `vendor/`, so there is no copy to drift: `composer update waynestate/creed` is the whole refresh. `--policy` and `BOOSTER_POLICY` still override it for one run.

`.env.example` holds the placeholder. Booster reads no secrets, makes no network calls of its own and talks to no Citadel host. Everything it prints from an app (file names, diffs) has control characters stripped.

When Rector runs, Booster passes it a few `BOOSTER_*` variables of its own (the app path, the sets, the PHP target). They are internal; do not set them.

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/hops.html

## Hops[#](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/hops.html#hops)

This page lists every hop Booster knows; the list is generated from the hop data by the docs build.

| Hop | Kind | From | To | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `php-55-to-56` | php | 5.5 | 5.6 | Move PHP 5.5 code to PHP 5.6. |
| `php-56-to-70` | php | 5.6 | 7.0 | Move PHP 5.6 code to PHP 7.0. |
| `php-70-to-71` | php | 7.0 | 7.1 | Move PHP 7.0 code to PHP 7.1. |
| `php-71-to-72` | php | 7.1 | 7.2 | Move PHP 7.1 code to PHP 7.2. |
| `php-72-to-73` | php | 7.2 | 7.3 | Move PHP 7.2 code to PHP 7.3. |
| `php-73-to-74` | php | 7.3 | 7.4 | Move PHP 7.3 code to PHP 7.4. |
| `php-74-to-80` | php | 7.4 | 8.0 | Move PHP 7.4 code to PHP 8.0. |
| `php-80-to-81` | php | 8.0 | 8.1 | Move PHP 8.0 code to PHP 8.1. |
| `php-81-to-82` | php | 8.1 | 8.2 | Move PHP 8.1 code to PHP 8.2. |
| `php-82-to-83` | php | 8.2 | 8.3 | Move PHP 8.2 code to PHP 8.3. |
| `php-83-to-84` | php | 8.3 | 8.4 | Move PHP 8.3 code to PHP 8.4. |
| `php-84-to-85` | php | 8.4 | 8.5 | Move PHP 8.4 code to PHP 8.5. |
| `laravel-5.8-to-6` | laravel | 5.8 | 6 | Move a Laravel 5.8 app to Laravel 6. |
| `laravel-6-to-7` | laravel | 6 | 7 | Move a Laravel 6 app to Laravel 7. |
| `laravel-7-to-8` | laravel | 7 | 8 | Move a Laravel 7 app to Laravel 8. |
| `laravel-8-to-9` | laravel | 8 | 9 | Move a Laravel 8 app to Laravel 9. |
| `laravel-9-to-10` | laravel | 9 | 10 | Move a Laravel 9 app to Laravel 10. |
| `laravel-10-to-11` | laravel | 10 | 11 | Move a Laravel 10 app to Laravel 11. |
| `laravel-11-to-12` | laravel | 11 | 12 | Move a Laravel 11 app to Laravel 12. |
| `laravel-12-to-13` | laravel | 12 | 13 | Move a Laravel 12 app to Laravel 13. |
| `phpunit-9-to-10` | phpunit | 9 | 10 | Move PHPUnit 9 tests to PHPUnit 10. |
| `phpunit-10-to-11` | phpunit | 10 | 11 | Move PHPUnit 10 tests to PHPUnit 11. |
| `phpunit-11-to-12` | phpunit | 11 | 12 | Move PHPUnit 11 tests to PHPUnit 12. |
| `phpunit-12-to-13` | phpunit | 12 | 13 | Move PHPUnit 12 tests to PHPUnit 13. |
| `phpunit-to-9-manual` | phpunit | below-9 | 9 | Move PHPUnit to ^9 by hand: PHPUnit below 9 does not run on PHP 8, so later gates cannot run until it moves. |
| `cas-to-sesame` | sesame | wayne-cas | sesame | Swap the wayne-cas package for SESAME using its compatibility classes. |
| `wayneui-1-to-2` | wayneui | 1 | 2 | Move WayneUI 1.x (Bootstrap 3) to 2.x (wsu- classes): rewrites the one-to-one items and lists the rest. |
| `node-pin-24` | node | any | 26 | Pin the app to Node 26: set engines.node in package.json and write .nvmrc. |
| `mix-to-vite` | node | laravel-mix | vite | Move a simple Laravel Mix front end to Vite (simple webpack.mix.js files only). |
| `vite-major` | node | any | 8 | Move a Vite front end onto Vite 8: pin vite and the Laravel and Vue plugin packages to the data versions. |
| `tailwind-3-to-4` | node | 3 | 4 | Move a Tailwind CSS 3 front end to Tailwind CSS 4 with the official upgrade tool. |
| `typescript-major` | node | any | 6 | Move the app to TypeScript 6: pin typescript in package.json, and vue-tsc too when the app has it. |
| `vue-26-to-27` | node | 2.6 | 2.7 | Move a Vue 2.6 front end to Vue 2.7, the last Vue 2 release, which carries the Vue 3 reactivity API. |
| `vue-27-to-compat` | node | 2.7 | 3 | Move a Vue 2.7 front end to Vue 3 through the @vue/compat build. |
| `vue-compat-codemod` | node | 3-compat | 3 | Run the vue-upgrade-tool codemod over the front end and keep every manual item it lists. |
| `vue-2-to-3` | vue | 2 | 3 | Move a Vue 2 front end to Vue 3 (playbook only; Rector does not read Vue). |
| `inertia-2-to-3` | node | 2 | 3 | Move an Inertia 2 app to Inertia 3: pin inertiajs/inertia-laravel to ^3.0 and @inertiajs/vue3 to ^3.0. |

> Every other hop lifts the engine; `wayneui-1-to-2` is the one that repaints the bodywork.

Booster plans any target the policy knows. A target past security support is allowed as a stop on the way up, with a plan warning that names the date its security support ended. A version the policy does not list at all is still refused by name.

---

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/proof.html

## Real output, from Booster's own example apps

Captured on 2026-11-04 with Booster 1.8.3. Each app below is one of the example apps in the `examples/` folder. A dry run changes nothing. This page is regenerated each release.
